surfaces.part: wood plank floor tile (full 64x16 flat texture)

answer.evidence: The image is a seamless terrain tile of light oak floorboards, 64 px wide and 16 rows tall, fully opaque with width 64 on every row. It has horizontal plank seams, dark gaps and a few nail-head or knot pixels, and it shows no standing body, no front face, and no top/front split. The column scans show only alternating plank tones (L 103-182) with no eave line or ellipse. Because it is a flat terrain texture and not a standing object, the top/front-face rules do not apply, so it reads as 'other' (a floor texture).

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a wood-plank floor with staggered boards. The seams and edges are a tinted dark brown, and the measured 0% near-neutral dark edge share agrees. That differs from the paving reference, whose outlines are 80% neutral. The measured 5x5 flat-fill coverage is 0%, and the boards carry grain dashes and a few speckle pixels. The median of 10 colours per tile matches the Beodeul median and exceeds the paving reference's 7. It reads as hand-shaded wood rather than a sticker, so a careful artist would accept it next to the paving reference. The main weakness is that the grain and per-board variation are a little sparse.
